Who Receives Technical Violations?

Who receives technical violations?

  1. What proportion of youth on probation supervision receive a technical violation during a probation term? How does this vary across race/ethnicity, sex, age, and risk level?

  2. What proportion of violations filed by a PO are rejected by supervisor or prosecutor?


1. Technical Violations Overview

NOTE: All analysis of technical violations in this section (e.g., supervision episodes with at least one technical violation) refers to the filing of any technical violations regardless of outcome/disposition.

### unique youth, referrals, and supervision episodes
df_technical_violations_race <- df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(race_clean) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(`Unique Youth (N)` = n_distinct(unique_id),
            `Unique Referrals (N)` = n_distinct(unique_referral_id),
            `Unique Supervision Episodes (N)` = n_distinct(unique_referral_id),
            `Supervision Episodes, Percent of Sample (column %)` = scales::percent(`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`/unique_supervision_episode_denom,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one technical violations (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_referral_id[technical_violation_flag==1])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one technical violations (RRI to White youth)` = round((n_distinct(unique_referral_id[technical_violation_flag==1])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`)/0.1184573, digits = 1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one new offense violation (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_referral_id[new_offense_violation_count>0 & !is.na(new_offense_violation_count)])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one new offense violation (RRI to White youth)` = round((n_distinct(unique_referral_id[new_offense_violation_count>0 & !is.na(new_offense_violation_count)])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`)/0.0261708,digits = 1)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Race/Ethnicity` = race_clean)

3. Supervisor/Prosecutor Rejections

Business Rule: According to Dallas County, all of the technical violation records without a referral number indicate that a PO filed the violation, but that it was rejected by a supervisor.

NOTE: Only about 2% of all violations fit this criteria – not sure if it warrants analysis (especially anything disaggregated). The Dallas team mentioned several factors to consider regarding rejections in general as well as the small percentage of violations that appear in our sample. A fair amount of informal rejection is possible (possible violations are rejected/not approved before any data would be entered or a violation would actually be filed). PO has to get permission from supervisor before filing a violation so there should be very few rejected violations (i.e., PO’s will likely only formally file a violation if they feel confident it will be approved by a supervisor).Thus, 2% really only reflects what is in the data system but likely does not speak to the real trend.
